definitions: A material for making fences, walls, etc., consisting of a network of stakes and branches.
A fleshy, pendulous process, usually brightly coloured, hanging from the head or neck of certain birds (e.g., a turkey or chicken) or other animals.
A genus of Australian trees and shrubs of the pea family, typically having yellow flowers.
examples: The fence was made of wattle and daub.
The turkey's wattle was a vibrant red.
Acacia trees are commonly known as wattles in Australia.
